title: GRACE Satellites
subtitle: Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment
description: NASA's GRACE and GRACE-FO twin satellites measure tiny changes in Earth's gravity field caused by shifting water mass. When aquifers deplete, less mass = lower gravity = detectable signal from orbit. GRACE data revealed India lost 109 km³ of groundwater between 2002–2008 in the Indo-Gangetic Plain alone.
detail: Data resolution: ~450 km. Monthly measurements. Free via NASA Earthdata.

title: Digital Water Level Recorders
subtitle: IoT Telemetry from 22,000+ Wells
description: CGWB has installed over 22,000 Digital Water Level Recorders (DWLRs) across India — sensors in observation wells that measure water depth every 15 minutes and transmit data via GSM/4G to a central server. This replaces once-a-quarter manual dipping with real-time alerts.
detail: Data flows into India-WRIS at indiawris.gov.in for public access.

title: GIS Dashboards & India-WRIS
subtitle: Web-Based Water Resources Information
description: The India Water Resources Information System (India-WRIS) integrates GRACE satellite data, DWLR sensor readings, rainfall records, and basin-level hydrology into an interactive GIS dashboard accessible to states, districts, and the public. It powers CGWB's assessment of 6,762 units.
detail: Includes aquifer maps, groundwater quality data, and trend charts by basin.

title: AI & Predictive Forecasting
subtitle: Machine Learning for Aquifer Futures
description: Researchers are applying LSTM neural networks and random forest models to GRACE + DWLR + rainfall datasets to predict water table levels 3–12 months ahead. CGWB and IITs are piloting AI-based 'groundwater weather forecasts' to give farmers and planners early warning of drought-stress.
detail: Early models achieve 85–92% accuracy in seasonal prediction for key aquifer zones.
